name: More customers buy their own launch (rideshare bottleneck after 2028)
market_basis: Dedicated share rises from 7 % to 12 % (middle of the 10–14 % BryceTech sees in the West): +5 pp × 17.9 t ÷ 700 kg × 12 M EUR
share_basis: Same win share as the core
note: Trigger: SpaceX limits commercial rideshare bookings after 2028 (reported, not confirmed)

name: Dedicated launches to polar and sun-synchronous orbits (Andøya)
market_basis: Q1 SAM 17.9 t (v_q1_funnel) × 7 % buying a dedicated launch ÷ 700 kg per full load × 12 M EUR per launch = 1.79 loads
growth_basis: Warehouse outlook 9 % p.a. (Novaspace, BryceTech); small-launch reports say 12–13.5 % (low reliability), so 9 % is conservative
share_basis: Isar's win share against Rocket Lab (assumption som_win_share)
margin_basis: Rocket Lab launch gross margin 2025: 81.3 / 199.0 M USD (10-K)
cost_basis: Pad lease and factory already committed (sunk)
note: Equals the Q1 SOM in revenue terms (9.7 M EUR)

name: Selling engines to other launchers
market_basis: Liquid rocket engine market 8.2 bn USD (Market Intelo, low reliability, includes captive engines)

name: Suborbital hypersonic test flights
market_basis: Europe assumed at 25 % of Rocket Lab's US HASTE volume: 190 M USD for 20 flights over 4 years = 47.5 M USD a year × 25 %
share_basis: Team: Andøya test range at hand; Hypersonica flies its own rocket there
cost_basis: Team: suborbital variant of Spectrum about 10 M EUR
note: Costs Andøya slots (30 a year for the whole site)

name: European institutional launches (ESA European Launcher Challenge)
market_basis: ESA ministerial 2025 subscribed 902.2 M EUR for launch services and upgrades to about 2030 = 180 M EUR per year over 5 years
share_basis: Isar's contract 197.8 M EUR of 902.2 M EUR subscribed (RFA 186.9, PLD 158.9, MaiaSpace pending)
margin_basis: Launch gross margin; part of the money funds upgrades (development), so this is an upper bound
cost_basis: Contract conditional on reaching orbit by end-2027 and upgrades by end-2028
note: Overlaps a little with the institutional satellites already in the core market (3.1 t)

name: Medium-lift rocket (2–20 t, partly reusable)
market_basis: Team: 10 % of global commercial launch revenue (12.4 bn USD, SIA 2026) is open to a new European medium launcher (rest SpaceX, captive, China)
share_basis: Team: against Falcon 9 (74 M USD), Neutron (50 M USD target), Ariane 6 (82 M EUR), MaiaSpace
cost_basis: Neutron cost about 360 M USD by end-2025 (CFO); Ariane 6 3.7 bn EUR; team 400 M EUR
note: Earliest after 10 launches a year at 90 % success (trigger assumptions)

name: Extras on every launch (integration, insurance brokerage, multi-orbit drop-off)
market_basis: Team: extras worth about 10 % of the dedicated launch market
margin_basis: Team: service revenue with little material cost

name: Own orbital transfer vehicle
market_basis: OTV market 2025: 1.9 bn USD (Global Market Insights, low reliability, broad scope)
share_basis: Team: D-Orbit, Impulse (525 M USD raised) and Exotrail are ahead and are Isar's customers

name: Own constellation and data services
market_basis: Earth-observation data 2.2 bn + value-added services 3.2 bn USD (2024, Novaspace) × 1.07
margin_basis: Planet Labs GAAP gross margin FY2026
note: Direct conflict with Planet and ICEYE, Isar's anchor customers

name: Building satellites (Rocket Lab model)
market_basis: Global satellite manufacturing revenue 2025: 20.4 bn USD (SIA 2026)
share_basis: Team: new entrant; Rocket Lab Space Systems reached 402.8 M USD (2 % of the market) after years
margin_basis: Rocket Lab Space Systems gross margin 2025: 125.9 / 402.8 M USD (10-K); OHB EBITDA margin 9.2 %
note: Not counted: lost launch business from customers like Planet, OHB and ICEYE who would face a competitor

name: Low inclinations and GTO from Kourou
market_basis: GCAT open market 5–45° that fits Spectrum, mean of 2024 (3.24 t) and 2025 (2.59 t) = 2.92 t × 7 % ÷ 700 kg × 12 M EUR
share_basis: Team: Diamant complex shared by five laureates
cost_basis: Team: fees not public; assumed about a third of Nova Scotia's

name: Mid-inclination orbits 45–90° from Nova Scotia
market_basis: GCAT open market 45–90° that fits Spectrum, mean of 2024 (6.25 t) and 2025 (3.69 t) = 4.97 t × 7 % ÷ 700 kg × 12 M EUR
share_basis: Same win share as the core
cost_basis: Site fee 3.75 M USD per quarter (13.4 M EUR a year), waived for 30 months after the first year; counted from start for simplicity
note: Already contracted. Canada's DND leases its own pad at the same spaceport (CAD 20 M a year): a possible anchor customer

name: Paid launch readiness for European states
market_basis: Proxy: US Tactically Responsive Space request FY2025 30.05 M USD (two Victus missions; Victus Sol 21.8 M USD). Europe publishes no budget; Sweden (FMV, SEK 209 M for launch capacity at Esrange) and Canada (DND, CAD 20 M a year for its own pad) show demand forming
growth_basis: Team: 15 % a year (range 10–25 %); Germany plans 35 bn EUR for space security by 2030 without naming a launch share, so the ramp stays conservative
share_basis: Team: Isar is the first European small launcher in orbit; RFA, PLD and MaiaSpace compete
margin_basis: Launch gross margin; readiness fees may earn more, not counted
cost_basis: Team: rocket on stock and standby crew about 5 M EUR a year; integration hall and stock about 20 M EUR
note: The biggest lever and the least certain one; see the sensitivity in the wiki
